Subject: Third-party manifest + planned decommission for LogRay telemetry

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG and SOC2 refresh we need a consolidated manifest of all subprocessor dependencies that interact with customer telemetry (both ingestion and telemetry-forwarding). In particular, we're tracking a vendor called "LogRay" that was previously used by several partners for edge telemetry collection. Can you confirm whether Redwood still has any active integrations or API keys for LogRay and, if so, provide: 

- a current subprocessor manifest (CSV acceptable) listing service, purpose, data categories, and residency
- any planned timeline to remove/decommission LogRay or mitigate (technical/workflow controls)
- a short attestation (one paragraph) we can store against the SIG record stating Redwood's status and next steps

We primarily need the manifest and a decommission timeline by EOD Monday (2026-10-05) to stay on our artifacts schedule. If you have a short runbook or artifact that describes the decommission steps, that would be perfect.

Appreciate it — Michael
Security Ops, CeraWell Analytics

Rachel / Karthik — pulled the artifacts and ran a quick sweep. Summary below and attached artifacts: redwood-subprocessors-manifest-20261001.csv (full roster), sig-lite-answers-cerawell.pdf (short SIG/CAIQ pointers), and logray-decommission-runbook-20261003.docx (technical steps).

Summary findings:
- Current state: We have one legacy API key tied to a sandbox telemetry stream used only by a 2019 partner PoC (tag: partner-poC-telemetry). No production customers use LogRay; the key was not used in the last 18 months.
- Data residency: the PoC stream resides in us-west-2 and no customer PII was routed to LogRay during the PoC period (we have logging to prove this).
- Controls: access is limited to a single service account; access logs are retained (S3) and covered by our SOC2 logging control. The manifest csv includes the service account and last-access timestamp.

Planned decommission timeline & steps (high level):
1) 2026-10-05: Revoke sandbox API key (non-prod) and snapshot any retained telemetry for audit (owner: infra-eng).
2) 2026-10-06: Update partner PoC config to point to Teleflux (our supported telemetry proxy) and run a validation sweep (QA).
3) 2026-10-07: Remove provider entry from runtime registry and update subprocessor manifest + CAIQ/SIG entries (compliance).
4) 2026-10-08: Produce attestation paragraph and contribute runbook + evidence to the SIG bundle.

I've included the runbook which contains command snippets used for key revocation and telemetry re-routing. Karthik — can you schedule infra-eng to perform the revocation step on 10/05? Also, I've drafted a short attestation below — Rachel, feel free to edit: 

Attestation (draft): "Redwood Inference confirms that LogRay was used solely for a 2019 non-production partner proof-of-concept. There are no active production integrations with LogRay. Redwood has revoked non-production access and will complete a decommission process by 2026-10-08; related evidence (access logs, snapshots, and runbook) will be included in our SIG/SOC2 bundle."

If that looks good I'll attach the CSV and send to Michael with the runbook.

—Marissa
